arxiv-2101-11261.title: On event-by-event pseudorapidity fluctuations in relativistic nuclear interactions
arxiv-2101-11261.creator: M. Mohisin Khan
arxiv-2101-11261.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by M. Mohisin Khan. Present study is an attempt to have a detailed look into event-by-event(e-by-e) pseudorapidity fluctuations of the relativistic charged particles produced in 28 Si-nucleus interactions at incident momenta 4.5A and 14.5A GeV/c. The method used in the present study makes use of a kinematic variable which is derived in terms of the average pseudo-rapidity and the total number of particles produced in a single event. The multiplicity and pseudorapidity dependence of these fluctuations have also been studied.

arxiv-2103-15542.title: Prediction of electronic and half metallic properties of Mn 2 YSn (Y = Mo, Nb, Zr) Heusler alloys
arxiv-2103-15542.creator: S. Zeffane ? , ?, M. Sayah ? , ?, F. Dahmane ? , ?, M. Mokhtari ? , ?, L. Zekri ? {}^{\textsf{\footnotesize{\mbox{?}}}}, R. Khenata ? {}^{\textsf{\footnotesize{\mbox{?}}}}, N. Zekri ? {}^{\textsf{\footnotesize{\mbox{?}}}}
arxiv-2103-15542.description: Abstract We investigate the structural, electronic and magnetic properties of the full Heusler compounds Mn 2 YSn (Y = Mo, Nb, Zr) by first- principles density functional theory using the generalized gradient approximation. It is found that the calculated lattice constants are in good agreement with the theoretical values.

arxiv-2303-12219.title: Jordan Algebras over icosahedral cut-and-project quasicrystals
arxiv-2303-12219.creator: Daniele Corradetti, David Chester, Raymond Aschheim, Klee Irwin
arxiv-2303-12219.description: Abstract . In this paper present a general setting for aperiodic Jordan algebras arising from icosahedral quasicrystals that are obtainable as model sets of a cut-and-project scheme with a convex acceptance window. In these hypothesis, we show the existence of an aperiodic Jordan algebra structure whose generators are in one-to-one correspondence with elements of the quasicrystal.

arxiv-2405-14524.title: QoE-Aware and Secure UAV-Aided Rate-Splitting Multiple Access Based Communications
arxiv-2405-14524.creator: Abuzar B. M. Adam, Xiaoyu Wan, Mohammed Saleh Ali Muthanna
arxiv-2405-14524.description: Abstract In this work, we address the issue of quality of experience (QoE) in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) aided multiuser rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) networks under secrecy constraints. The problem is formulated as maximization of sum mean opinion scores (MOSs) of the users. The problem is decomposed into two subproblems, beamforming and rate allocation and UAV trajectory subproblem.

arxiv-2408-07662.title: The spin-one Duffin-Kemmer-Petiau equation revisited: analytical study of its structure and a careful choice of interaction
arxiv-2408-07662.creator: M. Baradaran, L.M. Nieto, L.P. de Oliveira, S. Zarrinkamar
arxiv-2408-07662.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by M. Baradaran, L.M. Nieto, L.P. de Oliveira, S. Zarrinkamar. The Duffin-Kemmer-Petiau equation is investigated for spin one bosons with the so-called natural (normal) and unnatural (abnormal) parity states for non-minimal vector interactions. To illustrate the current state of knowledge about the equation, a thorough but concise discussion is made on what can be achieved analytically within this framework for well-known phenomenological interactions, including Coulomb, soft-core, Cornell, Kratzer, and exponential type interactions.

arxiv-2506-03001.title: Dynamic Fee for Reducing Impermanent Loss in Decentralized Exchanges
arxiv-2506-03001.creator: Irina Lebedeva 1 , Dmitrii Umnov 2 , Yury Yanovich 1 , Ignat Melnikov 1 , George Ovchinnikov 1 3
arxiv-2506-03001.description: Abstract Decentralized exchanges (DEXs) are crucial to decentralized finance (DeFi) as they enable trading without intermediaries. However, they face challenges like impermanent loss (IL), where liquidity providers (LPs) see their assets’ value change unfavorably within a liquidity pool compared to outside it.

arxiv-2506-20626.title: Task Allocation of UAVs for Monitoring Missions via Hardware-in-the-Loop Simulation and Experimental Validation
arxiv-2506-20626.creator: Hamza Chakraa, François Guérin, Edouard Leclercq, Dimitri Lefebvre
arxiv-2506-20626.description: Abstract This study addresses the optimisation of task allocation for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) within industrial monitoring missions. The proposed methodology integrates a Genetic Algorithms (GA) with a 2-Opt local search technique to obtain a high-quality solution. Our approach was experimentally validated in an industrial zone to demonstrate its efficacy in real-world scenarios.

arxiv-2507-02784.title: Quasinormal modes of Floquet media slabs
arxiv-2507-02784.creator: Benjamin Vial, Richard V. Craster
arxiv-2507-02784.description: Abstract Exploiting non-Hermitian wave-matter interactions in time-modulated media to enable the dynamic control of electromagnetic waves requires advanced theoretical tools. In this article we bridge concepts from photonic quasinormal modes (QNMs) and time-varying metamaterials providing the foundation for designing dynamic optical devices with prescribed scattering properties.

arxiv-2508-11189.title: Novel Parasitic Dual-Scale Modeling for Efficient and Accurate Multilingual Speech Translation Thanks: † Yanmin Qian is corresponding author
arxiv-2508-11189.creator: Chenyang, Yinfeng, Huiyan, Manhong, Yutao, Xingyang, Yanmin
arxiv-2508-11189.description: Abstract Recent advancements in speech-to-text translation have led to the development of multilingual models capable of handling multiple language pairs simultaneously. However, these unified models often suffer from large parameter sizes, making it challenging to balance inference efficiency and performance, particularly in local deployment scenarios.

arxiv-2510-14686.title: xLLM Technical Report
arxiv-2510-14686.creator: Tongxuan Liu, Tao Peng, Peijun Yang, Xiaoyang Zhao, Xiusheng Lu, Weizhe HuangZirui Liu, Xiaoyu Chen, Zhiwei Liang, Jun Xiong, Donghe Jin, Minchao Zhang,Jinrong Guo, Yingxu Deng, Xu Zhang, Xianzhe Dong, Siqi Wang, Siyu Wu, Yu Wu,Zihan Tang, Yuting Zeng, Yanshu Wang, Jinguang Liu, Meng Kang, Menxin Li
arxiv-2510-14686.description: Abstract We introduce xLLM , an intelligent and efficient Large Language Model (LLM) inference framework designed for high-performance, large-scale enterprise-grade serving, with deep optimizations for diverse AI accelerators. Current mainstream inference frameworks face practical challenges. On the one hand, enterprise-grade serving struggles with hybrid and dynamic workloads, strict demand for high availability of services, and distributed storage management.

pmc-10819845.title: Knowledge, attitude, and practice towards hepatitis B virus among healthcare workers: a cross-sectional, hospital-based study in Montserrado County, Liberia
pmc-10819845.creator: Bluefin Masell Freeman, Sampson Chea, Bode Ireti Shobayo
pmc-10819845.description: Prevention is critical in safeguarding against the spread of hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection. The knowledge, attitudes, and practices of healthcare workers (HCWs) regarding the disease play an important role in its prevention or spread, yet in this regard, data in Liberia remains scarce. Hence, determining the Knowledge, Attitude, and Practices (KAP) level of HCWs toward HBV infection becomes necessary.

pmc-11714046.title: Performance of plasma biomarkers for diagnosis and prediction of dementia in a Brazilian cohort
pmc-11714046.creator: Luis E Santos, Paulo Mattos, Thaís Pinheiro, Ananssa Silva, Claudia Drummond, Felipe K Sudo, Fernanda Barros‐Aragão, Bart Vanderborght, Carlos O Brandão, Sergio T Ferreira, Fernanda Tovar‐Moll, Fernanda G De Felice, IDOR Memory Clinic Initiative
pmc-11714046.description: BackgroundDementia is a growing concern throughout the developing world and is severely underdiagnosed among the Brazilian population. Despite remarkable progress in the biomarker field in recent years, local testing and validation of plasma biomarkers of AD and dementia is still lacking in Brazil and Latin America.

pmc-12402313.title: Computational investigation of mechanical properties and adsorption behavior of sulfur-doped h-BN nanosheets
pmc-12402313.creator: Azadeh Ghahremani, Zahra Tavangar, Mohammad Reza Zamani Seyfikar
pmc-12402313.description: Doping h-BN surface with sulfur has been shown to enhance its efficiency in photocatalytic reactions. Here, using density functional theory calculations, the various configurations of S-doped h-BN were investigated in terms of their formation energy, mechanical properties, structural, thermodynamic, and electronic properties, as well as their ability to adsorb metal atoms and hydrogen molecule.

pmc-12438363.title: An experimental study on the use of BERS-2 test to diagnose behavior and emotion: (a model for teenagers)
pmc-12438363.creator: K.-U. Mijgee, Y. Amanbyek
pmc-12438363.description: IntroductionThis study focuses on studying the most common psychological and physiological phenomena of adolescents, which directly and indirectly affect adolescent behavior and emotions, especially school children, using the BESR-2 test. Youth and peer pressure, crime, family and school stress, drug use, alcohol use, smoking, rape, theft, etc., create anxiety and psychological causes for teenagers in our society.

pmc-12641884.title: Leveraging community engagement and human-centered design to develop multilevel implementation strategies to enhance adoption of a health equity intervention
pmc-12641884.creator: Maggi A Price, Patrick J Mulkern, Madelaine Condon, Marina Rakhilin, Kara Johansen, Aaron R Lyon, Lisa Saldana, John Pachankis, Sue A Woodward, Kathryn M Roeder, Lyndsey R Moran, Beth A Jerskey

An urgent health equity problem in the U.S. is the mental health of transgender youth.

pmc-12653766.title: The Social Relevance of Numbers: Insights from Animal Studies
pmc-12653766.creator: Matteo Macchinizzi, Arianna Felisatti, Rosa Rugani, Yoh Iwasa
pmc-12653766.description: Number processing offers significant adaptive advantages, enabling animals to navigate their environment and maximize survival outcomes. Extensive evidence across species demonstrates that numerical cognition is a ubiquitous cognitive trait that enhances fitness by supporting critical behaviors such as foraging, hunting, and intergroup conflict.

pmc-13052447.title: Identification of Brimonidine as a Novel Substrate of Organic Cation Transporters OCT2 and MATE1 Expressed in Human Eye
pmc-13052447.creator: Charlotte Kölz, Claudia Neul, Ute Hofmann, Julia C. Dressler, Daniela Süsskind, Bernd Wissinger, Matthias Schwab, Anne T. Nies
pmc-13052447.description: PurposeBrimonidine, a selective α2-adrenergic agonist, is widely used in topical therapy for ocular hypertension or primary open-angle glaucoma. However, effective delivery is hindered by multiple ocular surface barriers. Because brimonidine is a cationic drug, we hypothesized that organic cation transporters (OCTs) and multidrug and toxin extrusion proteins (MATEs) are involved in brimonidine uptake in the human eye.

pmc-13482860.title: QTL rich genomic clusters in wheat: a catalogue for resistance to Puccinia striiformis f. sp. tritici
pmc-13482860.creator: Cyrus Micheni, Davinder Singh, Robert F. Park, Laura Ziems
pmc-13482860.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Wheat stripe/yellow rust, caused by Puccinia striiformis f. tritici (Pst), remains one of the most significant constraints to global wheat production. Genetic resistance breeding is the most effective, economical, and environmentally sustainable strategy for controlling stripe rust. Over the past two decades, advances in genome sequencing, molecular markers and high-throughput genotyping have led to the reporting of numerous Yr genes and an even greater number of quantitative trait loci (QTL, QYr).

pmc-13509273.title: Mapping the Distribution and Depth of Metacognitive Processes in Generative AI-Assisted Learning: Evidence from Interaction Logs and Concurrent Think-Aloud Protocols
pmc-13509273.creator: Shijin Li, Junjian Liu
pmc-13509273.description: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly used as a cognitive aid in education, yet no single process measure captures how learners monitor and control GenAI-assisted work. Guided by a reciprocal monitoring-control account of metacognition, this descriptive, exploratory study examined what interaction logs and concurrent think-aloud speech make observable during a 90 min instructional-design task.
